pages.outcome: Configure one UltimaBase application and understand how it is started, used, and isolated.
Predict create-input presence, default resolution, and complete persisted values.
Define a typed embedded object and know when it is not a separate schema.
Choose a field family, look up its builder, and understand which values are stored, accepted as input, or returned as output.
Construct, inspect, and use immutable draft and persisted schema models.
Choose and declare pointers and relations, then read or change membership through includes, filters, and link commands.
Define and register a schema, choose its declaration options, and understand when its fields and application handle become available.
Define a virtual field and predict its selection, privacy, typing, and failure behavior.
Express precise scalar, list, pointer, and structured predicates with valid operands.
Return a bounded, explicitly ordered Core page without inventing a cursor contract.
Choose a read terminal, build its input, and handle read failures in the correct application context.
Load and filter related data, including request-contextual relation views, without mistaking a filter for authorization.
Choose between inclusive and exclusive projections and the appropriate singular terminal.
Identify the error owner and handle FrameworkError without exposing internal details.
Understand safe persistence rewrites without changing policy or Hook meaning.
Place validation, policy, Hooks, persistence, and post-commit work correctly.
Use Master deliberately without creating a transport-forgeable bypass.
Add request identity values without creating an authority mode or implicit grant.
Place each security requirement at the boundary that actually enforces it.
Use bulk commands with the same guarantees as their singular forms.
Create one record with defaults, a nested pointer command, and an exact result type.
Choose schema-root or loaded-model deletion and interpret its result.
Choose legal pointer and relation commands and verify their atomic order and limits.
Place business work and post-commit effects on the correct side of commit.
Update by identity or unique predicate and handle a possibly absent target correctly.
Build deterministic upserts without broad filter or nested-write ambiguity.
Declare a plugin with definePlugin, test it in an application, and choose the extension boundary for its behavior.
Decide whether a schema option is a feature or a rule, and declare each with definePlugin or Core's plugin contracts.
Choose a schema contribution and type its fields, rules, and commands from the plugin source.
Declare executable plugin behavior and choose its exact public transport surface.
Select the correct lifecycle, Runtime, storage, and security boundary for an advanced plugin.
Understand how community plugins will be listed without confusing visibility with official maintenance.
Define fail-closed authorization that can only narrow as policies compose.
Protect individual objects with public, principal, and role permissions.
Register a User, manage its session, and expose authentication through your chosen transport.
Compose role membership with Access or ACL without treating membership as a grant.
Configure the PostgreSQL plugin, choose a direct schema policy, and diagnose startup failures.
Declare a dimension-safe vector field and recognize the current physical storage limit.
Soft-delete a record, verify that ordinary reads hide it, restore it, and purge it from trusted server code.
Install the GraphQL packages you need, configure execution, and understand HTTP and explorer boundaries.
Configure the HTTP foundation, its defaults, application routes, CORS, rate limits and pre-dispatch handling.
Run an UltimaBase HTTP application on a managed or existing Hono server without mixing listener and browser-policy ownership.
Call generated REST routes while preserving the same Runtime semantics as TypeScript.
Choose and configure the right Hook phase for input, mutation, or post-commit behavior.
Decide when application validation belongs in the Validation plugin rather than Core or Hooks.
Decide whether a feature belongs in the application plugin chain and know what Core validates.
Add the smallest compatible plugin set and verify its application-local behavior.
Verify a public create-and-read path with an isolated application and disposable PostgreSQL schema.
Identify the checks your application and deployment must pass before public exposure.
Identify the failed startup boundary and repair it without bypassing a safety check.
Type-check your application with TypeScript 7 and keep TypeScript 6 for tools that need its JavaScript API.
Choose the packages you need and verify their runtime and plugin compatibility.
Decide whether the current pre-release framework is suitable for evaluation or adoption.
Find proposed capabilities and their roadmap context without mistaking them for commitments.
Choose a contribution path, verify your work, and submit a useful proposal or pull request.

standalonePages.outcome: Understand the product promise and choose a next step.
Understand UltimaBase's core model and choose the right next path.
Understand the generated project's first-run path and use manual installation until packages are published.
Start and verify a minimal schema-backed PostgreSQL application from a manually configured project.
Place plugins, schemas and the application in the files that keep every schema module loadable.
